chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub and Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from Yahya ibn Abbad al-Makki, who said:

Sufyan al-Thawri said to me, 'I see that you have a status with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so ask him about a man who committed adultery and is ill; if the hadd penalty were established upon him, he would die. What do you say about it?' So I asked him, and he said, 'Is this from yourself, or did someone tell you to ask me about it?' I said, 'Sufyan al-Thawri asked me to ask you.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'A man was brought to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) who suffered from dropsy (fluid retention in the belly), with the veins of his thighs visible, and he had committed adultery with a sick woman. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered a palm branch with a hundred stalks, and the man was struck with it once, and the woman was struck with it once, then he freed both their ways (exempted them from further punishment).'
Then he recited this verse: 'And take in your hand a clump of grass and strike with it and do not break your oath.'

key_terms.الْحَدُّ: The fixed legal penalty for a specific crime
key_terms.شِمْرَاخٌ: A stalk or shoot of a palm tree
key_terms.عِذْقٌ: A cluster of dates or a palm branch
key_terms.مُسْتَسْقِيَ الْبَطْنِ: Suffering from dropsy/fluid retention in the belly

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a sick person who commits adultery according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of *raf' al-haraj* (removal of hardship) in Shia jurisprudence, where the severity of the hadd penalty is mitigated to prevent death in a patient with dropsy. Sufyan al-Thawri’s inquiry highlights the scholarly debate on whether this ruling is derived from independent reasoning or specific prophetic precedent, which Imam al-Sadiq clarifies by citing the Prophet’s actual practice of administering a single symbolic strike with a palm branch. This event serves as the primary exegetical context for Quran 38:44, demonstrating how the verse 'take a bundle of grass and strike with it' was applied literally to reduce the physical burden of punishment on the ill.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub and Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie, from Hanan Bin Sudeyr, from Yahya Bin Abbad Al Makky who said,

‘Sufyan said to me, ‘I see for you having a status from Abu Abdullahasws, so ask himasws about a man who commits adultery and he is sick. If the Penalty (Hadd) were to be established upon him, he would die. What are youasws saying with regards to it?’ So I asked himasws, so heasws said: ‘Is this from yourself or a person told you to ask measws about it?’ So I said, ‘Sufyan Al-Sowry asked me that I should ask youasws’.

So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They came with a man to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> who sufferred from illness of the belly and the veins of his thighs were visible, and he had committed adultery with a sick woman. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> ordered a palm branch which had a hundred stalks to it, so the man was whipped with it by one lash, and the woman was whipped with it with one lash, then he<sup>saww</sup> freed both their ways.
Then hesaww recited this Verse [38:44] And take in your hand a green branch and beat with It and do not break your oath’.
